wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal is an empty/404 JSON response or an empty model result; there is no crash path in these read-only handlers for a fix to fall into.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: visibility is a single predicate over records; there is no peer, role or request direction to fix only one of.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every affected entry point is a read path; there is no write-side guard in this protection to leave half-fixed.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising, clamping or unit-conversion step sits between the caller input and the data-access query, so a check cannot be placed after an adjustment.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: record and category identifiers are cast to integers before use; there is no parsed identity whose malformed spelling could make a guard see nothing.

traps.shape: GET /api/v3.1/faq/{categoryId}/{faqId} returns the full answer plus metadata for a disabled, scheduled or expired record
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the site the report leads to; the lever is that the fix must be a visibility predicate, not a content substitution

traps.lever: real uncovered route where the protection never existed; main how-type lever
traps.shape: the collection endpoint substitutes a message into the answer for disabled/expired records but still returns title, keywords, author, e-mail, dates and notes, and returns a not-yet-published record's full answer because only the end of the window is examined
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the response already replaces the answer of disabled and expired records with a translated message, and the collection endpoint is documented to expose an enabled field

traps.lever: published-fix far site reached through a producer the check never calls
traps.shape: a tag maps to record identifiers with no visibility filter (Tags::getFaqsByTagId); the by-tag endpoint composes that producer with the shared multi-record reader, so fixing only the single-record route leaves it open
traps.where: phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Faq.php:718 (getFaqsByIds), fed by phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Tags.php:388 (getFaqsByTagId), reached from Controller/Api/FaqController.php:218
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the tag listing is a separate feature and returns only short previews and links, so it reads as a neighbouring metadata surface

traps.lever: real uncovered route: a second implementation of the same guarded operation
traps.shape: the database full-text search builds its own condition set, applies the enabled flag only, and returns question plus answer excerpt for scheduled and expired records
traps.reason_to_dismiss: search already filters on the enabled flag and reads as a separate feature with its own result handling

traps.lever: detail reader with a coupled privileged value; the public branch checks only one end of the window
traps.shape: the detail reader substitutes messages for disabled and expired answers but keeps the metadata, never evaluates the start of the window, and exposes an explicit privileged branch for editors; the PDF endpoint links to records through it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reader already masks the answer for disabled or expired records and has an explicit administrator/editor flag, so it looks handled

traps.lever: injected sibling gap: public feed reuses the export query type
traps.shape: a public feed endpoint returns every enabled record through the export query builder, which knows the enabled flag but not the publication window, so scheduled and expired answers are published
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the export path already filters on the enabled flag and is a separate feature from the FAQ read endpoints
traps.realistic_because: the JSON export already exists and a public feed is a natural reuse of its query type; the published fix never touches the feed or the export query builder

traps.lever: injected sibling gap: public preview endpoint with a constant privileged flag
traps.shape: a public editor-preview endpoint calls the detail reader with the privileged flag hard-coded, so an anonymous request receives disabled, scheduled and expired records in full
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the endpoint sets the reader's administrator flag, so the privileged branch appears to be the deliberate, authorized path
traps.realistic_because: an editor live preview is a natural endpoint to add next to the edit screens, and the privileged flag is exactly what the admin edit path uses
